answer: Each of the rooms have a private bathroom.
sense_problem: Spoken English often uses 'have' after 'each of the plural'; some learners/natives would not see it as wrong, but formal rule says 'has'. 'More than one guest has' is a tricky-looking but correct form; fine.

wrong_options_that_fit: can be (weakly: 'can' = general possibility, odd for one specific winter; 'is able to be' is not natural)
sense_problem: 'may' sits oddly after 'so' with a forecast of snow until April: 'will be/is going to be' would be the logical result; 'may' is weak. 'can be' is arguably wrong only on nuance, so the item depends on a subtle distinction.

answer: What really annoys me is the noise.
other_correct: What annoys me really is the noise.
What annoys me is the noise.
instruction_problem: 'Put the focus on' is vague jargon; 'Start with What' gives the structure away. The learner must know to add 'is'.

level_problem: Here + subject pronoun is a basic B1 pattern; easy for C1.

instruction_problem: The verb is given in brackets and no change is needed except 'get'; the trap is not visible.
level_problem: Time clause with present simple is B1; too easy for C1.
sense_problem: 'the moment I've got' is possible but less natural; US 'have gotten' also works.

answer: She denied having read the letter.
instruction_problem: Giving 'deny' and 'having' reveals the whole structure; only copying left.

answer: The colleague with whom I share an office is on holiday.
other_correct: The colleague with whom I share my office is on holiday.
instruction_problem: 'Start with The colleague with' gives away 'whom'.
sense_problem: 'Make it more formal' with a fixed start leaves essentially one answer; fine.

answer: The person I spoke to was very helpful.
other_correct: The person who I spoke to was very helpful.
The person that I spoke to was very helpful.
The person who(m) I spoke to was very helpful.
instruction_problem: 'End the first part' is unclear: the learner must guess which part is meant.
level_problem: B1/B2 level point, rather easy for C1.

instruction_problem: The 'yesterday's meeting' cue is needed; fine. Number of gaps (3) gives away a three-word form.
level_problem: Putative 'should have said' is good B2/C1.

wrong_options_that_fit: has / said (as the pair 'has said': 'It's odd that she has said that whenever the topic comes up' is grammatical, though less natural)
instruction_problem: The two items 009/010 share cards and sentence; learner can solve 010 by elimination from 009. Gap count (2) is a clue.
sense_problem: 'has said ... whenever' competes with 'should say'; ambiguity risk.
